How local files follow each other. Spotify streams always change with a short fade.
Each song ends, then the next one starts.
The end of a song fades into the next one.
Mixes like a DJ: on the beat, at the end of a phrase, tempos matched. The mix shows on the seek bar and the cover pulses with it.

Quick mix brings the next song in from its start on the next downbeat. Real mix picks a downbeat or phrase of this song within 4 seconds and the best entry of the next one, over 4 bars with the bass swap.
No mix between songs that follow each other on their album: they run into each other as on the record.
Show the mix in the player
The song coming in is named over the cover while the two overlap, and the cover pulses with the beat during the mix.
Optional overlap bounds in seconds. Minimum 0 is automatic; maximum 0 has no limit.
Enter 0–90 seconds and keep the minimum at or below the maximum.
Uses one analysis thread and prepares at most the current and next song. The mix algorithm stays the same.
How far the next song\'s tempo may be bent to land on the beat. Beyond it, the songs change with a filtered fade: the next one comes in without its bass, which takes over on its downbeat.
Bass swap and filters during the mix. Off, only the volumes move.
Beat blend matches the tempos where it can, else cuts on the beat or fades. Cut on the beat switches songs on a downbeat. Smooth fade fades without touching the tempo.
Short: 4 to 8 bars. Balanced: preferably 8 to 16. Long: preferably 12 to 32, up to 90 seconds. Shorter when the music needs it.
Songs in clashing keys get short mixes, matching keys long ones. Off, keys are ignored.
Off, podcast episodes and audiobooks start and end whole.
